data.name: Sita
data.gender_notes: Sita is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The one who is born from the furrow in the earth or the one who is the embodiment of purity, virtue and devotion. In Hindu mythology, Sita is the consort of Lord Rama and is considered the ideal wife and the epitome of chastity and devotion. The name Sita carries the meaning “Seat, Furrow” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Sita usually hope their child will grow to embody seat, furrow and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sita total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: Sita is an iconic figure in Indian literature and culture, often regarded as the perfect example of marital loyalty, relationship goals, and self-sacrifice. Tales of her abduction and rescue by her husband, Lord Rama, are told and retold through many Indian epics and folklore stories, passed down from generations. The Sita-Rama story is a popular motif for art, drama, and literature. Classic Indian films like Mughal-e-Azam and Jodhaa Akbar have drawn inspiration from Sita's story, and her character continues to influence the modern Indian consciousness and pop culture.
data.spiritual_significance: For Hindus, Sita represents the divine feminine aspect of god and is revered as a goddess in her own right. She is the embodiment of purity, and her devotion and self-sacrifice are held in high esteem. Sita, married to Lord Rama, is an illustration of the union between the divine masculine and feminine energies, which is believed to bring balance, harmony, and fulfillment to one's life. Her story teaches us the importance of love, devotion, and inner strength in facing challenges and traveling the path of dharma (duty and virtue).
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sita symbolizes the ideal woman, embodiment of purity, devotion and strength. She represents the power of unwavering love and loyalty, even in the face of adversity. Her name is derived from the Sanskrit word 'sita' meaning 'furrow' or 'auspicious'. It signifies the furrowed earth that nurtures new life, reflecting Sita's role as a nurturing and life-giving force.

historical_references.reference: Sita was the wife of Rama, an avatar of the god Vishnu, and is considered an ideal woman in Hinduism. The story of Rama and Sita is told in the epic Ramayana.

Sita is also believed to be the goddess of the earth, identified as the earth goddess Prithvi, in Hinduism. This belief is related to the idea of the earth as the mother of all life, and Sita is revered as the embodiment of this aspect of the goddess Prithvi.
